result:
Done — `js/plane.js` only, 30 insertions / 2 deletions, `node --check` passes.

**Root cause (confirmed, both halves measured numerically):** the podium parks at world x ≈ ±3.83 (`rx ≈ 0.485` from `main.js:95`) while the camera sits at x=0 — a 15.3° off-axis azimuth. At 1920×1080 the disc rim's projected left/right extremes sat **3.39° off level**. Of that, **1.68° is pure off-axis projection skew** (world verticals converge on the nadir, so anything off-centre reads rolled) and **1.71° is `PODIUM_TILT = .12` being a *world-X* pitch, which decomposes into apparent roll at that azimuth**. The orchestrator's primary hypothesis was right, and the secondary contributed the other half. No camera roll involved; I did not move the camera, so `toScreen`/`unproject` and all route maths (1685-1686, 2374-2377, 2972, 3338) are untouched.

**Fix:** `p.rig.rotation.set(PODIUM_TILT, spins[index], 0)` → `parkRig(p.rig, spins[index])` (new helper beside `PODIUM_R`). It builds the rig quaternion as `roll(-skew about the view ray) × tilt(PODIUM_TILT about the camera-relative *horizontal* axis) × spin(world Y)` — so the deck still tips toward the viewer by the same 6.9° (the disc doesn't flatten into a sliver) but picks up no apparent roll, and the residual projection skew is cancelled. Measured rim roll after: **-0.27°** at 1920×1080, **-0.24°** at 1280×800 (the leftover is the finite-radius term, invisible). It reads off `rig.position`, so it self-corrects per section, per side (mirrored sections get the mirrored correction), and unwinds to zero as the home podium slides to centre stage for the game. The parked plane inherits it for free via `groundQ.copy(p.rig.quaternion)` in `groundPose`; airborne banking is computed from `airQ` on a separate path and is not touched.

**Responsive strategy:** `scale` now fits to whichever axis runs out — `mobile ? min(halfW/3.2, halfH/3.2) : min(halfW/5.4, halfH/2.4)`, clamped `[.5, 1.35]` mobile / `[.8, 1.75]` desktop. The key fact is that with a fixed 35° vertical fov the visible world *height* is constant regardless of window height, so the stranded vertical space was width-derived `scale` throwing away headroom that never shrank. 390×844 goes .569 → .641; a 844×390 landscape phone goes .80 → 1.35 (fits: 2.88+3.02 < halfW 9.60 across, 2.218+2.16 < halfH 4.436 up). Desktop is unchanged — `halfH/2.4 = 1.848` sits above the existing 1.75 cap.

**Risk — read this:** `Flight.layout.scale` still wins whenever `main.js` has run, which is always in the real page, so **Task 2 only takes effect in the fallback path**. I kept that contract deliberately rather than breaking it, because `main.js:92` derives the podium diameter `D` (and from it the CSS `--col`) from the *same* formula — overriding `scale` here without changing `stageLayout()` would desync the 3D podium from the content column. **To make the responsive win real, whoever owns `main.js` must port the identical `min(halfW/3.2, halfH/3.2)` / `min(halfW/5.4, halfH/2.4)` rule into `stageLayout()` at line 91.** Second, smaller risk: `camRight`/`camUp`/`camFwd` are captured once from `camera.quaternion`, valid because the camera is set at lines 34-35 and never rotates again — if a later agent animates camera orientation, those three must move inside `parkRig`.

**Visually verify:** (1) podium rim and plane wings level on every section, both left- and right-hand sides — the right-side sections should now lean the opposite way from before, i.e. not at all; (2) the deck still reads as a disc with visible top face, not a flat sliver (confirms the tilt was re-aimed, not deleted); (3) scroll a full hop and confirm the plane still banks into its turns and rolls level only on touchdown; (4) trigger the dogfight on section 0 and watch the podium slide to centre — it should stay level throughout the slide; (5) resize to a short/landscape phone window and confirm the plane fills the height without the disc clipping the screen edge.
